question: Did learned positional embeddings beat sinusoidal positional encodings in the Transformer experiments, and why did the authors keep the sinusoidal version?
answer: 3.5 Positional Encoding Since our model contains no recurrence and no convolution, in order for the model to make use of the order of the sequence, we must inject some information about the relative or absolute position of the tokens in the sequence [Attention Is All You Need, arXiv:1706.03762v7, p. 6, Section 3.5 Positional Encoding]. To this end, we add "positional encodings" to the input embeddings at the bottoms of the encoder and decoder stacks [Attention Is All You Need, arXiv:1706.03762v7, p. 6, Section 3.5 Positional Encoding]. The positional encodings have the same dimension dmodel as the embeddings, so that the two can be summed [Attention Is All You Need, arXiv:1706.03762v7, p. 6, Section 3.5 Positional Encoding]. There are many choices of positional encodings, learned and fixed [9] [Attention Is All You Need, arXiv:1706.03762v7, p. 6, Section 3.5 Positional Encoding]. In this work, we use sine and cosine functions of different frequencies: PE(pos,2i) = sin(pos/100002i/dmodel) PE(pos,2i+1) = cos(pos/100002i/dmodel) where pos is the position and i is the dimension [Attention Is All You Need, arXiv:1706.03762v7, p. 6, Section 3.5 Positional Encoding].

The positional encodings have the same dimension dmodel as the embeddings, so that the two can be summed [P1]. There are many choices of positional encodings, learned and fixed [9] [P1]. In this work, we use sine and cosine functions of different frequencies: PE(pos,2i) = sin(pos/100002i/dmodel) PE(pos,2i+1) = cos(pos/100002i/dmodel) where pos is the position and i is the dimension [P1].

question: Which dataset gave Moshi its full-duplex ability, and what property of that dataset made it suitable?
answer: 5.6 Quality and statistics of generated dialogues Metrics [Moshi: a speech-text foundation model for real-time dialogue, arXiv:2410.00037v1, pp. 30-31, Section 5.6 Quality and statistics of generated dialogues]. Beyond single-turn question answering, we evaluate the linguistic quality of the generated dialogues by scoring them with an external language model, while also looking at turn-taking metrics [Moshi: a speech-text foundation model for real-time dialogue, arXiv:2410.00037v1, pp. 30-31, Section 5.6 Quality and statistics of generated dialogues]. We follow the methodology of Nguyen et al. (2023) [Moshi: a speech-text foundation model for real-time dialogue, arXiv:2410.00037v1, pp. 30-31, Section 5.6 Quality and statistics of generated dialogues]. The turn-taking metrics are defined as follows: Inter-Pausal Units (IPU) are continuous streches of speech that are separated by a silence of at least 0.2s on each side [Moshi: a speech-text foundation model for real-time dialogue, arXiv:2410.00037v1, pp. 30-31, Section 5.6 Quality and statistics of generated dialogues]. Pauses are silences between IPUs of the same speakers [Moshi: a speech-text foundation model for real-time dialogue, arXiv:2410.00037v1, pp. 30-31, Section 5.6 Quality and statistics of generated dialogues].

question: What frame rate and bitrate does the Mimi codec operate at, and how many quantizers does it use?
answer: To improve the ability of Mimi to encode speech into compact representations while reconstructing high-quality audio, we add Transformer modules in the bottleneck, one right before quantization and one after [Moshi: a speech-text foundation model for real-time dialogue, arXiv:2410.00037v1, pp. 10-11, Section 3.3.1 Architecture]. These Transformers have 8 layers, 8 heads, RoPE position encodings, a finite context of 250 frames (20 seconds), GELU (Hendrycks and Gimpel, 2016a) activations, a model dimension of 512 and an MLP dimension of 2048 [Moshi: a speech-text foundation model for real-time dialogue, arXiv:2410.00037v1, pp. 10-11, Section 3.3.1 Architecture]. To stabilize training, we use LayerScale (Touvron et al., 2021), with initialization of the diagonal values at 0.01 [Moshi: a speech-text foundation model for real-time dialogue, arXiv:2410.00037v1, pp. 10-11, Section 3.3.1 Architecture].
answer_raw: To improve the ability of Mimi to encode speech into compact representations while reconstructing high-quality audio, we add Transformer modules in the bottleneck, one right before quantization and one after [P1]. These Transformers have 8 layers, 8 heads, RoPE position encodings, a finite context of 250 frames (20 seconds), GELU (Hendrycks and Gimpel, 2016a) activations, a model dimension of 512 and an MLP dimension of 2048 [P1]. To stabilize training, we use LayerScale (Touvron et al., 2021), with initialization of the diagonal values at 0.01 [P1].
